chunk_a.text_snippet:
Title: UK politics Q&A, as it happened: Andrew Sparrow answers your questions on Starmer, Reform and more
Date: 2026-04-02

Content: (Zack Polanski, unlike Keir Starmer, is passionate about PR.) A Reform UK government if the rise in the Green splits the progressive vote. Do you believe Starmer actually wants the UK to rejoin the EU or are he’s closer ties speeches just trying to win back people who have switched to the LibDems and Green who do actually want to rejoin. I don’t think Starmer thinks rejoining is realistic. He might be right. But until about 2013 you would have said leaving wasn’t realistic either. BeaconHill71 asks: Q&A - Is the Guardian making any efforts to archive the liveblogs, and make them accessible/searchable in future? A minute-by-minute account of some of the events from the past decade or so would be an invaluable resource for future historians, but as with all digital media, there’s a risk of all this insight being lost if it’s not actively preserved. Yes. You can find more than more than 3,500 of them here. This is from Manchemec.

chunk_b.text_snippet:
Title: UK politics: Starmer warns ‘lot of work to do’ to make ceasefire permanent at start of talks in Gulf - as it happened
Date: 2026-04-08

Content: 12.30pm: Richard Tice, Reform UK’s deputy leader, and Malcolm Offord, the party’s leader in Scotland, hold a press conference in Aberdeen. Afternoon: Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, is on a visit in London. At some point today the Welsh Liberal Democrats are launching their Senedd election campaign. If you want to contact me, please post a message below the line when comments are open (between 10am and 3pm), or message me on social media. I can’t read all the messages BTL, but if you put “Andrew” in a message aimed at me, I am more likely to see it because I search for posts containing that word. If you want to flag something up urgently, it is best to use social media. You can reach me on Bluesky at @andrewsparrowgdn.bsky.social. The Guardian has given up posting from its official accounts on X, but individual Guardian journalists are there, I still have my account, and if you message me there at @AndrewSparrow, I will see it and respond if necessary.

Guardian liveblog format and reader engagement

initial_question.rag_input: How does Andrew Sparrow use his role on the Guardian liveblog to manage reader engagement regarding Reform UK's political strategy as discussed on April 2 and April 8, 2026?
initial_question.question: How does Andrew Sparrow use his role on the Guardian liveblog to manage reader engagement regarding Reform UK's political strategy as discussed on April 2 and April 8, 2026?
initial_question.answer: Andrew Sparrow manages engagement by inviting readers to post messages "below the line" between 10am and 3pm, specifically suggesting they include his name to ensure he sees them. This method facilitates direct interaction as he covers the activities of Reform UK leadership, such as Richard Tice and Nigel Farage's events on April 8, while also utilizing the liveblog platform—which he noted on April 2 has over 3,500 entries—to provide ongoing political analysis and archive these discussions for future reference.
initial_question.bridging_topic: Connecting Sparrow's engagement methods with his coverage of Reform UK strategy.
